title: Argentinian Yeast Empanadas
description: Delicious, yeasty, and savory, these empanadas are perfect for a crowd. They are a pescatarian-friendly twist on traditional Argentine cuisine.
instructions: Combine flour, salt, sugar, and yeast in a large mixing bowl.
Add the egg and mix until a dough forms.
Knead the dough for 10 minutes until it becomes smooth and elastic.
Place the dough in a greased bowl, cover it with a damp cloth, and let it rise in a warm place for 1 hour.
On a lightly floured surface, roll out the dough to a thickness of 1/8 inch.
Cut out circles of dough using a cookie cutter or the rim of a glass.
Place a tablespoon of the onion, horseradish, and cure mixture onto the center of each dough circle.
Fold the dough in half over the filling and press the edges together with a fork to seal the empanada.
Place the empanadas on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper and brush the tops with a little water.
Bake for 20 minutes or until the empanadas are golden brown.
